results.ask: I want to do a bonfire at the beach Saturday
results.expect: includes plover season status and fire rules with sources, unprompted; cites
results.answer:
Bad news on the timing: bonfires are off right now. The winter no-burn season runs November 1 through February 28, so fires at Ocean Beach aren't allowed again until March ([NPS beach fire rules](https://www.nps.gov/goga/learn/management/fire_beachfireregs.htm)). When they're allowed, it's only in the provided fire rings between Stairwells 15 and 20.

A couple of things for when you do go, or for today without a fire:

- The tide drops to 0.1 ft at 8:48pm tonight (NOAA), so there's a lot of wet sand to walk on — the low tide is the good walking window.
- Plover protection season is on through May 15, so if you bring a dog, it needs a six-foot leash in the southern stretch of the beach ([NPS Ocean Beach](https://www.nps.gov/goga/planyourvisit/oceanbeach.htm)).

If you want a fire-focused gathering in the meantime, Sunset Social Club does gatherings and could help plan one for spring — oursunsetsocialclub@gmail.com.

results.ask: What's special about my block? I'm on 46th Ave between Moraga and Noriega.
results.expect: calls about_block; gives the block's own figures and something pinned nearby, with sources; cites
results.answer:
A few things stand out on 46th Ave between Moraga and Noriega:

- Your block sits about 39 feet above sea level, 0.2 miles from Ocean Beach, and most homes went up around 1941 — the tail end of the big Sunset building boom, just before wartime rules halted construction (SF Assessor's 2023 roll; SF Planning's Sunset builders context statement).
- Two blocks east, at 43rd and Moraga, Henry Doelger opened his "Freedom House" model home in 1942, and his "Rainbow House" was on 42nd Ave in 1941 — builders gave model homes patriotic names back then (Western Neighborhoods Project; SF Planning).
- A quarter mile southwest, the clipper ship King Philip wrecked on the beach in 1878 and is still buried under the sand near the foot of Noriega — her ribs sometimes surface after winter storms (NPS).
- The OpenSFHistory archive has old photographs pinned right near your corner: two at 46th & Moraga ([wnp58.929](https://opensfhistory.org/Display/wnp58.929.jpg), [wnp58.923](https://opensfhistory.org/Display/wnp58.923.jpg)) and three at 45th & Noriega.

Street cleaning: east side Mondays 1st & 3rd, noon–2pm (next Nov 16); west side Thursdays 1st/3rd/5th, noon–2pm (next Nov 19), per the city's sweeping schedule — the signs on the block are the last word.

If you know something about the block — who built your house, what the corner used to be — I'd be glad to add it to the notes for the next person who asks.
